## Claims
- [computed] In degrees \(6,7,8,9,10\), claim-1 reports quotient free ranks \(1,1,2,1,1\), respectively, and no torsion. [artifact 621a26ec7b4419d76351b43e22fff9df644945c6458e2a531d2542a0819b6602]
- [proved] Quotient rank and torsion do not determine ordered \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) transition matrices.

## Strategy
Let \(Q=\mathbb Z^2\), presented as \(M/L\) with \(M=\mathbb Z e_1\oplus\mathbb Z e_2\) and \(L=0\). Thus
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z^2,\qquad \operatorname{rank}Q=2,\qquad \operatorname{Tor}(Q)=0.
\]
Fix \(G_L=(e_1,e_2)\), and use
\[
[g_{L,r}]=\sum_c T_{r,c}[g_{R,c}].
\]

For \(G_R^{(I)}=(e_1,e_2)\),
\[
T^{(I)}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det T^{(I)}=1.
\]
For \(G_R^{(S)}=(e_2,e_1)\),
\[
e_1=0e_2+1e_1,\qquad e_2=1e_2+0e_1,
\]
hence
\[
T^{(S)}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det T^{(S)}=-1.
\]
Both marked situations have exactly the same quotient invariants
\[
(\operatorname{rank}Q,\operatorname{Tor}(Q))=(2,0),
\]
and both transition matrices have Smith diagonal \((1,1)\), but
\(T^{(I)}\ne T^{(S)}\). Thus even quotient rank, torsion, and transition Smith data do not recover transition coordinates.

The rank-one boundary also does not determine the sign: for
\(Q=\mathbb Ze\), \(G_L=(e)\), the choices \(G_R=(e)\) and \(G_R=(-e)\)
give transition matrices \((1)\) and \((-1)\), respectively, with the
same quotient invariant \((1,0)\). Only the zero-rank boundary forces the
empty \(0\times0\) transition matrix.

Therefore the rank/torsion portion of claim-1 determines only the abstract degreewise quotient groups (for degrees \(6\)--\(10\), \(\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z^2,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z\)); it contains no marked-basis coordinate information from which \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) matrices can be deduced.

## Gaps
None for this logical non-determination certificate. It does not compute any transition matrix or assert any parent theorem.
